newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed weaker as profit-taking wiped out gains made on Monday and Tuesday morning, analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index shed 4.66 points, or 0.46 percent, to 1,018.01, after peaking at 1,033.09 earlier. The small-capitalised Second Board gained 1.09 points to 536.35.
"We saw the normal profit-taking. It was pretty much expected," said Jonathan Duckett, research analyst at Mohaiyani Securities.
Index heavyweights Tenaga and Telekom led the falls, shedding 20 and 30 cents respectively.
Dealers said they had seen foreign funds buying Malaysian blue-chips cheapened in recent weeks following a rise in short-term interest rates.
Share prices had risen since Monday on support by local institutional funds. Analysts said this could have been a show of support ahead of the return of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday.
The release of central Bank Negara's reserves on Tuesday showed a sharp fall after its defence of the ringgit against speculators.
Mahathir had left Malaysia for a two-month sabatical in May.

Bank Negara's foreign currency reserves fell to 61.9 billion ringgit as at July 15, 1997, compared to 70.71 billion ringgit at June 30. The reserves fell primarily due to the bank's defence of the ringgit, which had hit a 38-month low against the U.S. dollar, two weeks ago.

Infrastructure developer Renong gained 12 cents to 3.44 ringgit on active trading. Analysts said the company may benefit from a possible relaxation of rules governing property purchases by foreigners, as announced by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Friday.
Volume stood at 244 million shares valued at 1.74 billion ringgit. Losers edged out gainers 296 to 290.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot July contract dropped 14.0 points to 1,016.0 with 1,446 contracts traded. August futures shed 15.0 points also to 1,016.0, with 137 lots traded.
